ruled_out_vectors.vector: C1: FullMath.mulDiv phantom overflow — mulDiv(max,max,max) and near-overflow boundary inputs
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: FullMath.mulDiv uses 512-bit intermediate via assembly. Tested mulDiv(uint256.max, uint256.max, uint256.max) = uint256.max, mulDiv(uint256.max, 1, 1) = uint256.max, and (2^128-1)^2/2^128. Halmos symbolic check also ran (timeout due to assembly complexity, but no counterexample found).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C2: mulDivRoundingUp not always >= mulDiv
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz tested with 10,000 runs across full uint128 range. mulDivRoundingUp >= mulDiv holds universally, difference always <= 1. Halmos symbolic check PASS (check_roundingUpAlwaysGtOrEq).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C3: FixedHelper.calculateFixedSwapByRatio edge cases — zero input, 1 wei, max uint128, asymmetric ratios
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All edge cases tested: zero input -> zero output, 1 wei at 1:1 -> 1 wei, 1:2 ratio -> 200 for 100 input (forward) and 50 (reverse), max uint128 at 1:1 -> max uint128. All pass.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C4: FixedHelper._calculateSwapByInputFixed — zero liquidity height, max fee
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SwapByInput path uses calculateFixedSwapByRatioRoundingDown (rounds down for output, favoring protocol). Zero liquidity reverts via FixedPool__InsufficientExpectedReserve. Max fee (10000 BPS) gives amountRemainingLessFee=0, so amountOut=0. Tested in C13 fee tests.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C5: FixedHelper._calculateSwapByOutputFixed — output = full reserve, output = 0, output > reserve
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Output exceeding reserve reverts via FixedPool__OutputValidationFailed (L1626-1628). Output=0 produces no state changes. Full reserve output is bounded by expectedReserve calculation using calculateFixedSwapByRatioRoundingDown.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C6: Add+Remove liquidity round-trip rounding loss
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Round-trip tested at multiple ratios: 1:3 ratio with 1000e18 gives <= 2 wei loss. Fuzz tested with 10,000 runs across ratio space (r0,r1 in [1,3]). Round trip always loses or breaks even (back <= amount + 2).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C7: DynamicHelper.computeSwap loop invariants — fee growth monotonicity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee growth accumulation tested: 10 sequential fee increments with FullMath.mulDiv(feeAmount, Q128, liquidity) are additive and non-zero. Zero liquidity guard prevents division by zero. Cumulative fee growth verified.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C8: DynamicHelper._getTokensOwed uint128 truncation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested normal range (delta=1e18, liq=1e18: result fits uint128), max fee growth (delta=uint256.max, liq=1: result = uint128.max), and fuzz with realistic liquidity (up to 1e24). No truncation in realistic scenarios.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C9: DynamicHelper._updatePosition — 0 liquidity change fee-only collection
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee collection with 0 liquidity change is by design — modifyPosition allows delta=0 to collect fees without adding/removing liquidity. No state corruption observed.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C10: DynamicHelper._crossTick fee growth flip consistency
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Cross-tick uses unchecked wrapping subtraction: outside = global - outside. Fuzz tested: double-crossing restores original value for all uint256 inputs. This is identical to Uniswap V3's design.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C11: SqrtPriceMath.getNextSqrtPriceFromInput/Output direction and edge cases
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested: zero amount returns same price, zeroForOne=true decreases price, zeroForOne=false increases price, max amount with max liquidity doesn't revert, near MIN_SQRT_RATIO input works correctly.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C12: SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta/getAmount1Delta rounding direction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Equal prices give delta=0. Rounding up always >= rounding down for both amount0Delta and amount1Delta. Liquidity=1 gives small but non-zero amounts.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C13: SwapMath.computeSwapStep — amountRemaining=1, extreme fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 1 wei input with 0.3% fee: amountIn=0, feeAmount=1 (total consumed=1). Fee 99.99%: tiny output. Fee 0%: full amount, 0 fee. No free tokens invariant holds with 10,000 fuzz runs.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C14: TickMath round-trip at every 1000th tick
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested getSqrtPriceAtTick -> getTickAtSqrtPrice for every 1000th tick from -887000 to 887000 (1774 ticks). All round-trips exact. MIN_TICK and MAX_TICK boundary verified.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C15: BitMath.mostSignificantBit/leastSignificantBit edge cases
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All 255 powers of 2 tested for both MSB and LSB. MSB(0) reverts, LSB(0) reverts. MSB(uint256.max)=255, LSB(uint256.max)=0. MSB(1)=0, LSB(1)=0. Fuzz with 10,000 runs: MSB/LSB properties hold.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C16: LiquidityMath.addDelta underflow/overflow revert
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: addDelta(0, -1) reverts. addDelta(uint128.max, 1) reverts. Normal operations: addDelta(100, 50)=150, addDelta(100, -50)=50, addDelta(100, 0)=100, addDelta(0, 0)=0.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C17: FeeHelper input/output fee edge cases
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 100% input fee takes entire amount. 1 BPS on 10000 rounds up to 2. 9999 BPS output fee is non-zero. Fee=0 gives full amount. Tested both in fixed pool and dynamic pool contexts.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C18: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput rounding direction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput uses mulDivRoundingUp twice (L313-314), rounding UP for output. This favors the maker (gets more output). Tested in MathDeepDive.t.sol: 1 wei at 1:1 gives 1 wei, non-perfect price shows roundUp >= roundDown.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C19: SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96 overflow and edge cases
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Both zeros returns Q96. Zero amount1 returns MIN_SQRT_RATIO. Zero amount0 returns MAX_SQRT_RATIO. Equal amounts returns ~Q96 (within 0.1%). Overflow (uint256.max, 1) returns 0 per the while-loop fallback.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C20: SingleProviderHelper round-trip loss
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forward swap (mulDiv rounds down) then reverse (mulDivRoundingUp rounds up). Round trip at price=1.5: amountBack <= amountIn. Round trip with 1 wei at price=7/3: back2 <= 1. No value creation.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C21: Medusa on FixedPoolType
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Medusa v1.5.0 ran but could not find assertion/property tests (Medusa requires property_ prefix without arguments). Ran forge fuzz with 10,000 runs on all fuzz tests instead — all pass.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C22: Medusa on DynamicPoolType
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Same as C21. Medusa architecture requires stateless property tests. Ran forge fuzz with 10,000 runs on all dynamic pool tests instead — all 44 pass.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C23: INV-SW02 No Profitable Round-Trip
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fixed pool: forward (roundDown) then reverse (roundUp) at ratios 1:1, 1:2, 1:3 — back <= amount. Dynamic pool: fuzz tested INV_SW02 with 10,000 runs at 1:1 price, 0.3% fee — token0Returned < amount always.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C24: INV-SW03 Rounding Favors Protocol
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 1000 sequential 1-wei swaps at 3:7 ratio: protocol doesn't lose (reversedBack <= 1000). Rounding direction verified: roundUp >= roundDown across 5 different ratios. Fuzz: no value creation beyond 1 wei with 10,000 runs.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C25: INV-E01 Fee Monotonicity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee growth accumulation tested in C7: 10 sequential fee increments with FullMath.mulDiv are monotonically non-decreasing and additive. Dynamic pool sequential dust swaps (100 swaps) show totalInput >= totalOutput.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C26: Cetus-pattern precision extraction via tick_index overflow in computeRatioX96
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96 has a while-loop that reduces the multiplier exponent when amount1 * 2^(2*n) would overflow. When n reaches 0, the loop breaks. For uint256.max, the function returns 0 (overflow -> 0). This does NOT feed into DynamicPoolType — it's in hooks/SqrtPriceCalculator, used only for initial pool creation price. DynamicPoolType uses TickMath which validates tick range [-887272, 887272].

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C27: Balancer-pattern rounding direction in sequential dust operations
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 100 sequential 1-wei swaps at 1:2 ratio: total output reversed back requires <= totalInput. Pool balance never decreases. FixedHelper uses calculateFixedSwapByRatioRoundingDown for output (protocol-favorable). All rounding directions checked across withdrawLiquidity, addLiquidity, and swap paths.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C28: ERC-4626 first depositor inflation — SingleProviderPoolType and DynamicPoolType
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SingleProviderPoolType doesn't use shares — LP is the sole provider, reserves track directly. DynamicPoolType uses tick-range positions (not share-based), so donation doesn't inflate shares. Both pool types use reserve accounting, not share/asset conversion. The ERC-4626 pattern doesn't apply.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C29: Hook price manipulation — extreme price from SingleProviderPoolHook
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SingleProviderPoolType.swapByInput (L328-330) validates sqrtPriceCurrentX96 against MIN_SQRT_RATIO and MAX_SQRT_RATIO bounds. Hook price is accepted within those bounds, but the LP (pool creator) sets the hook, so a malicious hook is a self-inflicted config error (known FP pattern #4 from audit memory). Core's reserve checks (_safeDecrementUint128 for amountOut) also bound extraction.

theft_theses.thesis: Extract dust accumulated from swap rounding by front-running LP withdrawals
Manipulate SingleProvider hook price to extract value from LP reserves
Exploit empty-pool price snap to front-run and capture arbitrage
Exploit 100% fee asymmetry (input allows, output rejects) to create one-directional trap
Exploit +1 tolerance in swapByOutput to desync reserves from actual balances
Exploit swapByInput fallback to swapByOutput for better rate when reserves are low
Overflow consumedLiquidity via high-volume swapping to corrupt reserve calculations
Exploit redeposit overflow in withdrawLiquidity unchecked subtraction
Exploit stale pool state read in SingleProvider cross-contract pattern

hypothesis_results.detail: Dust per swap is bounded (<=10 for tested ratios). Dust accumulation is economically insignificant — gas cost of withdrawal exceeds dust value. First-withdrawer advantage is at most a few wei per swap.

consumedLiquidity underflow in _collectPositionSide: sideValue is computed from height range and decremented by 1 only when height.liquidity != height.remainingAtHeight. The subtraction liquidity - sideValue >= 1 always holds. consumedLiquidity is accumulated via _addLiquidity (L723) and only decremented in _collectPositionSide, maintaining invariant.

consumedLiquidity is uint256 and accumulates across swaps. FullMath.mulDiv handles uint256*uint256/uint256 correctly. Overflow of uint256 requires 2^256 swap volume — physically impossible. Even at 1e18 per swap, would require >1e59 swaps.

Hook price manipulation: LP sets the hook at pool creation, so a malicious hook is a self-inflicted config error (known FP #4). The hook is trusted by design. An exploitable hook vulnerability would be a separate finding in the hook contract, not in SingleProviderPoolType.

Empty-pool price snap: snapPrice requires no initialized ticks between current and target price. When liquidity is 0 and LP removes, attacker can snap but only to adjacent uninitialized region. Next LP adding liquidity at the manipulated price would need to provide tokens at that price. Core validates token amounts match position math. Attacker gains are bounded by the tick range they provide liquidity in.

Redeposit overflow in withdrawLiquidity: _calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights includes precisionAddLoss subtraction (L360-363, 376-378) which reduces redeposited amounts. The depth0ValueOf1 / depth1ValueOf0 calculations use RoundingDown, making redeposited values conservative. Unchecked subtraction is safe because redeposited <= value by construction.

100% fee asymmetry is intentional by design. Input allows MAX_BPS (takes everything), output rejects >= MAX_BPS. Consistent across all 3 pool types and Core's _getPoolFee. A dynamic fee hook returning MAX_BPS is a self-inflicted config error.

+1 tolerance in swapByOutput: totalAmountInFilled = amountIn + 1 triggers fee recalculation and Core's balance check at AMMModule L2208 verifies actual token balance. The 1-unit discrepancy causes revert at Core level. Cannot compound — each swap is independently balance-checked.

Stale pool state read: SingleProviderPoolType reads via getPoolState (view function) within the same external call from Core. Reentrancy guard (TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags) prevents concurrent state modifications. The view read is consistent within the call because no state-modifying operations occur between Core calling poolType and poolType calling Core.getPoolState.

SwapByInput fallback to swapByOutput: when amountOut > reserveOut, fallback caps output to reserveOut and recalculates amountIn via calculateFixedOutput (rounds UP). The check swapCache.amountIn > initialAmountIn (L49-50) prevents overcharging. The effective rate is the same because: input rate = amountOut/amountIn = (reserveOut)/(amountIn_recalculated). Fee structure is the same for both paths in SingleProviderHelper.
